terms.comment: Any pipe or tube, and in particular the shepherd’s pipe of reeds of falling length, Pan’s invention; Traupman (168) has it for any pipe.

phrases.latin: fistula, cui semper dēcrēscit arundinis ōrdō: nam calamus cērā jungitur usque minor
phrases.english: the pipe, in which the row of reeds keeps growing shorter: for each reed is joined with wax to a smaller one

phrases.latin: Opiliō (pāstor) pāscit gregem, īnstrūctus fistulā et pērā, ut et pedō
phrases.english: The shepherd feeds his flock, equipped with a pipe and a bag, and a crook too

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 168, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
